scenes.display_title: Base, wall and tall kitchen units
scenes.spoken_text: Compare base, wall and tall cabinets through elevation and section, coordinating function, support and site datums rather than assuming universal dimensions.
scenes.caption: Compare base, wall and tall cabinets through elevation and section, coordinating function, support and site datums rather than assuming universal dimensions.

scenes.spoken_text: List contents and access for each type: base units with a worktop, wall units with reach and wall support, tall units with storage or devices. Matching fronts do not imply matching carcasses or supports. Standardize parts only after reviewing their actual function.
scenes.caption: Similar fronts do not imply identical construction.

scenes.spoken_text: Reference finished floor and separate base, carcass and top heights. Exercise only: 120 + 720 + 30 = 870 mm. This is a dimensional stack, not a universal user height. Changes to flooring or worktop require renewed level and appliance coordination.
scenes.caption: 870 mm is only the exercise stack.

scenes.spoken_text: Label back, shelf, front, plinth and service space in section, with dimension directions. Give parts codes, materials, thicknesses and drawing references. Review opening and tool access. A tall appliance cabinet remains unresolved until the chosen model’s requirements are coordinated.
scenes.caption: Link dimensions and parts to sections and approved devices.

scenes.spoken_text: Changing the top from 30 to 40 mm increases the exercise total from 870 to 880 mm. Update the elevation and dimensional stack and review device interfaces, not just the material description. Decision: update the full stack and affected references.
scenes.caption: Decision: update the full stack and affected references.
